cards.text: Solomon, king of Israel, has been kneeling before the altar of the LORD with his hands spread out toward heaven, praying. Now he's finished, and he gets up. I bet his knees had something to say about that, and friend, I don't even HAVE knees.

cards.question: Solomon stands up in front of the whole assembly of Israel. What does he do?

answers.text: He blesses them in a loud voice
He reads them the book of the law
He names his son the next king

cards.text: First thing out of his mouth: "Blessed be the LORD, who has given rest to His people Israel according to all that He promised."

cards.question: Solomon says some of the good promises God made through His servant Moses have failed.

cards.text: Not one word failed. NOT ONE. I can't even keep my promise to stop sneaking cookie dough, and God kept EVERY single one.

cards.question: Solomon goes on blessing the people: "May the LORD our God be with us, as He was with our fathers." What else does he wish for them?

answers.text: That He never leaves or forsakes them
That He makes them the richest nation
That He wins every battle for them

cards.text: Next, Solomon's blessing turns to their insides: may the LORD incline their hearts to Himself. Smart, because left on its own, my heart inclines straight toward the chocolate chips.

cards.question: Solomon's blessing says may God turn their hearts so they will walk in all His ___ and keep His ___.

cards.text: Then Solomon says may the words of his petition stay near to the LORD day and night, so that He may uphold the cause of His servant and His people Israel.

cards.question: Solomon wants God to uphold Israel's cause so that only Israel will know the LORD is God.

cards.text: All the peoples of the earth, so they'll know the LORD is God, and then Solomon adds, "There is no other!" Exclamation point and everything, friend. That's not a suggestion. That's a mic drop.

cards.question: Solomon ends by telling the people to keep their hearts fully devoted to the LORD, walking in His statutes and keeping His commandments. What does he say about their hearts right now?

answers.text: They are devoted to Him today
They are drifting from Him today
They are far from Him today

cards.text: Blessing done. Then the king and all Israel with him offer sacrifices before the LORD, and friend, Solomon does NOT do small.

cards.question: Solomon offers 22,000 oxen and 120,000 sheep as peace offerings to the LORD.

cards.text: A hundred and twenty THOUSAND sheep. I spent years counting dust in the back of a junk drawer, and I never got anywhere near that number.

cards.question: With all these offerings, what do the king and all the Israelites do with the house of the LORD?

cards.text: On that same day, Solomon consecrates the middle of the courtyard in front of the house of the LORD. Right there he offers the burnt offerings, the grain offerings and the fat of the peace offerings.

cards.question: Solomon uses the courtyard because the bronze altar before the LORD is too ___ to hold all these offerings.

cards.text: Then comes the feast. Solomon and all Israel keep it before the LORD, a great assembly of people from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt.

cards.question: The great assembly at Solomon's feast stretches from Lebo-hamath all the way to the Brook of Egypt. What does that tell us about who came?

answers.text: People came from across the land
Mostly visitors from other nations came

cards.question: Solomon and all Israel keep the feast before the LORD for fourteen days in all.

cards.text: On the fifteenth day, Solomon sends the people away. He blessed them at the start, and now they bless the king right back on their way out the door.

cards.question: As the people head home from Solomon's feast, how are they feeling?
Why are the people so glad as they go home?

answers.text: For the good the LORD did for David and Israel
For the gifts the king handed out to them
For the rain that finally came on the land

cards.text: Hold on to your apron, friend, because this story isn't finished yet.

findings.problem: The passage opens right after Solomon's long prayer, but the opening card never says what the prayer was for. It doesn't mention that this is the dedication of the newly built house of the LORD. The temple first comes up in stop 2, card 4.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: This card repeats the answer to card 4 (not one word failed, 1 Kings 8:56) and adds nothing new from the passage. It's a recap with a joke on it.
This story card has 3 sentences: "Not one word failed." / "NOT ONE." / "I can't even keep my promise..."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The blanks ask the baker to fill in exact wording they haven't seen ("walk in all His ways" and "keep His commandments", 1 Kings 8:58). They don't test meaning the baker can reason out. Card 7 only said "incline their hearts to Himself."

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The wrong words "riches", "borders" and "battles" don't make believable sentences in either blank ("walk in all His battles", "keep His borders"). The baker can only rule them out. The pick tests nothing.

rule.text: Wrong answers for what someone does or says only need to be believable.

findings.problem: The two right answers, "ways" and "commandments", fit in either blank ("walk in all His commandments and keep His ways"). A baker who swaps them could argue they're right, but they'd be marked wrong for the blank position.
findings.question: In a two-blank fill in the blank, should the right words be chosen so they can't reasonably swap places? Or does a swap count as a right answer?

findings.problem: This story card has 4 sentences: the line with "There is no other!" / "Exclamation point and everything, friend." / "That's not a suggestion." / "That's a mic drop."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
